newsitem.title: USA: Freeze ends season for North Dakota crops.
newsitem.headline: Freeze ends season for North Dakota crops.

text.p: A freeze during the week ended Sunday halted the growing season for row crops in North Dakota, but dry conditions allowed farmers to complete small grains harvesting, according to the state's Agricultural Statistics Service.
Durum harvest was 88 percent harvested, behind last year and the average.
Corn, soybean and sunflower harvests were behind the average. Corn harvest was four percent finished versus 13 a year ago and the 20 average.
Soybeans were 43 percent harvested versus 53 a year ago and the 53 average. Sunflowers were five percent harvested versus 14 a year ago and the 12 average.

Corn and soybean conditions improved while sunflowers declined. Corn was rated 10 percent excellent, 44 good, 29 fair, and 17 poor. Soybeans were six percent excellent, 34 good, 36 fair and 24 poor. Sunflowers were rated 15 excellent, 58 good, 24 fair and three poor.
